title: Invention of the sail
summary: The sail is thought to have developed from watching wind act on a piece of cloth. Merchants on the Tigris and Euphrates could row or pole downstream easily, but had to fight the current coming back in small reed boats. With a sail, they could return far more easily. Mesopotamian inventions like this are dated to the Uruk or Early Dynastic periods. In Egypt, a boat in the Qa-a rock tableau is apparently the earliest known depiction of a sail.

as_recorded.calendar: Predynastic Egypt / Naqada II (Yale Egyptological Institute)

where.modern_name: Mesopotamia; stand-in pin at Uruk, Iraq

importance.justification: The sail put wind to work for moving people and goods over water.

related.because: The invention of the sail facilitated the expansion of southern Mesopotamian riverine and maritime trade networks across the Tigris, Euphrates, and Persian Gulf.
